items.title: Kaapi Co. — a coffee brand from the hills

results: Online sales up 3× in the first quarter
Shortlisted for a national design award

items.short_description: A warm, confident identity for a family estate in Chikmagalur moving from bulk beans to branded retail.
items.description:
Kaapi Co. had grown great coffee for three generations but sold almost all of it in bulk. We built a brand that carries the estate’s story onto shelves and into cafés: a hand-drawn bean mark, a palette taken from the soil and the roast, and a packaging system that scales from 250 g bags to wholesale sacks.

The approach

Two workshops on the estate, a week of café visits and a lot of tasting. The result is a brand that feels made by people, not a factory.

items.title: Paisa — a savings app for first jobbers

results: 32% of users set up a monthly goal in week one

items.short_description: Product design for a savings app that makes goals and spending simple for people in their first job.
items.description: Paisa wanted saving to feel like progress, not punishment. We interviewed forty young professionals, then designed a calm, high-contrast app with goals at its centre and a design system the in-house team now maintains.

items.title: SOMA — skincare packaging
items.short_description: Quiet, tactile packaging for a clean-skincare brand: recycled paper labels, clay tones and one bold wordmark.
items.description: The range needed to stand out on crowded shelves without shouting. We used soft clay tones, generous space and a single typographic system across eleven products.

items.title: Sound of the Hills festival
items.short_description: A loud, joyful poster system for a three-day music festival in the Nandi Hills.
items.description: Three stages, three shapes, three colours. The system let the festival team create more than 200 assets in-house from one simple kit.

items.title: BuildSchool website
items.short_description: A clear, friendly website for a coding bootcamp, built to turn curious visitors into students.
items.description: We rewrote every page with the team, simplified course choice to three paths and built the site so the marketing team can launch new cohorts without developers.

items.title: Bylane Brewing cans

results: Four core beers launched in cans

items.short_description: A bright, collectable can range for a craft brewery’s move from taps to shelves.
items.description: Each beer gets its own colour and symbol, held together by a single bold layout.

items.title: Tamarind restaurant identity

results: Opened to a six-week waiting list

items.short_description: An identity, menus and signage for a modern South Indian restaurant in Indiranagar.
items.description: A lowercase wordmark with a slight lean, a tamarind-orange palette and menus printed on recycled stock.

items.title: Wayfinding for a design campus
items.short_description: A clear, colour-coded sign system for a five-building campus.
items.description: Letters for buildings, colours for floors, arrows everyone understands.

items.title: Book covers for Ink & Leaf
items.short_description: A series of covers for new Indian fiction.
items.description: Simple shapes that hint at each story.

items.title: The New Normal — magazine cover
items.short_description: A cover illustration for a special issue on life after the pandemic.

items.question: How much does a brand identity cost?
items.answer: Most identity projects are between ₹4 and ₹15 lakh, depending on scope. We send a fixed quote after a first call.

items.question: How long does a project take?
items.answer: Usually 8 to 16 weeks from kick-off to launch files.

items.question: Do you work with startups?
items.answer: Yes — about half our clients are early-stage companies. We offer a lighter “launch kit” for pre-seed teams.

items.question: Can you work with our developers?
items.answer: Yes. We hand over design systems in Figma and work alongside in-house or partner developers.
